20.text: Nvidia is backstopping a $45B Anthropic cloud project, cosigning an Nscale data center loan, launching Nemotron 3.5 and Granary v2, and expanding Vera Rubin/CPU availability on Oracle Cloud. Meanwhile OpenAI plans to buy Google TPUs, the DOJ is scrutinizing Nvidia's $12.9B Hugging Face deal, and Nvidia reportedly restricted Chinese access via overseas data centers.

8.text: Nvidia is only mentioned incidentally as a top holding in broad Vanguard ETFs like VOO and VUG, whose tech and AI exposure drives their returns. The articles otherwise focus on recommending these funds for long-term, passive investing.

19.text: Nvidia will report Q3 fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 17, with expected revenue around $108 billion, roughly double year-over-year, after ten straight quarters of beating forecasts. Analysts debate whether the stock, down 15% from highs, will rise or fall post-earnings.

10.text: Memory demand is outpacing supply through 2029, with SK Hynix sold out and Micron locking in multi-year shipments; Micron co-designed its next chip with Nvidia. Articles frame Micron as cheap despite record results, though management sees no supply-demand balance timeline.

15.text: Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, TSMC and Lumentum are reported as AI chip rivals with strong AI revenue growth, raised outlooks, and supply constraints, while Broadcom shares fell on margin pressure. Nvidia is mentioned mainly as the incumbent these rivals are measured against.

11.text: Nebius fell 36% from September highs on AI-infrastructure funding concerns despite $40B+ in long-term contracts, while CoreWeave grew revenue 112% with a $104B backlog but faces high bond yields and costs. CoreWeave also added capacity in Denmark and planned Asia-Pacific and Middle East deployments.

12.text: S&P 500 valuations hit dot-com and 1929 extremes as AI spending and rate worries mount. Steve Eisman warns AI price cuts and slowing usage could trigger a correction and recession, though he calls a 2008-style crash unlikely.
